concepts.description_formal: For a function modelling a quantity, the derivative at an input is the instantaneous rate of change of that quantity with respect to its independent variable at that input.
concepts.description_plain: In a situation, the derivative says how fast the modelled quantity is changing at one instant.
concepts.name: The derivative as an instantaneous rate of change in context
concepts.notation: f prime of a as a rate at the instant a

concepts.description_formal: The unit for the derivative of f with respect to x is the unit for f divided by the unit for x, so a second derivative carries the unit of f divided by the square of the unit of x.
concepts.description_plain: The units of a derivative are the units of the function divided by the units of the independent variable.
concepts.name: Units of a derivative
concepts.notation: units of f per unit of x

concepts.description_formal: For a particle in rectilinear motion with position x of t, the velocity is the derivative of position and the acceleration is the derivative of velocity, which is the second derivative of position.
concepts.description_plain: Differentiating position gives velocity and differentiating velocity gives acceleration.
concepts.name: Position, velocity, and acceleration on a line
concepts.notation: x of t, v of t, a of t

concepts.description_formal: The velocity of a particle in rectilinear motion is a signed quantity whose sign gives the direction of motion, and the speed is the absolute value of the velocity.
concepts.description_plain: Velocity carries a sign that says which way the particle moves, and speed is its size with the sign removed.
concepts.name: Velocity, speed, and direction
concepts.notation: speed equals the absolute value of v of t

concepts.description_formal: The speed of a particle is increasing at an instant when its velocity and acceleration have the same sign at that instant, and decreasing when they have opposite signs; the sign of the acceleration alone does not settle the question.
concepts.description_plain: A particle speeds up when velocity and acceleration share a sign and slows down when their signs differ.
concepts.name: Speeding up and slowing down
concepts.notation: signs of v of t and a of t compared

concepts.description_formal: A contextual rate problem supplies a quantity as a function of an independent variable, and the question asks for a value of the function, a value of its derivative, or an interpretation of one of those values, with the vocabulary of the context rather than the vocabulary of motion.
concepts.description_plain: Problems about very different quantities share one structure: a function, its independent variable, and a derivative read as a rate.
concepts.name: The common structure of contextual rate problems
concepts.notation: rate of change of the named quantity

concepts.description_formal: In a related rates problem the quantities appearing in a geometric or contextual relation are functions of a common independent variable, ordinarily time, and the chain rule is the basis for differentiating each of them with respect to that variable.
concepts.description_plain: Each changing quantity is a function of time, so each one contributes its own rate when the relation is differentiated.
concepts.name: Variables in a related rates problem as functions of time

concepts.description_formal: A related rates setup requires an equation relating the quantities, drawn from a geometric formula, the Pythagorean theorem, a similar triangles proportion, or the context itself; reducing the number of variables before differentiating often makes the differentiation possible.
concepts.description_plain: Before anything can be differentiated, an equation has to tie the quantities together.
concepts.name: The relating equation

concepts.description_formal: A quantity that varies with time must be carried as a variable through the differentiation and replaced by its instantaneous value only afterwards; a quantity constant in time may be substituted at any stage.
concepts.description_plain: Values that hold only at one instant go in after the differentiation, not before.
concepts.name: Substitution after differentiation
concepts.notation: instantaneous values substituted into the differentiated equation

concepts.description_formal: The solution of a related rates problem is reported as a rate with the units of the quantity divided by the units of time, and its sign is interpreted as increase or decrease of that quantity in the situation described.
concepts.description_plain: The answer is a rate with units and a sign that says whether the quantity is growing or shrinking.
concepts.name: Interpreting a related rate in context
concepts.notation: units and sign of the reported rate

concepts.description_formal: The tangent line at a point is the graph of a locally linear approximation of the function near the point of tangency, so its value at a nearby input approximates the function value there.
concepts.description_plain: Near the point of tangency the tangent line and the curve are close, so the line's height approximates the function's value.
concepts.name: The tangent line as a local linear approximation
concepts.notation: y equals f of a plus f prime of a times the change in x

concepts.description_formal: The behaviour of the function near the point of tangency may determine whether a tangent line value is an underestimate or an overestimate of the corresponding function value; on an interval where the graph is concave up the tangent line lies below the curve, and on an interval where it is concave down the tangent line lies above.
concepts.description_plain: Whether the tangent line sits above or below the curve follows from how the curve bends.
concepts.name: Direction of the approximation error
concepts.notation: sign of the second derivative near the point

concepts.description_formal: When the ratio of two functions tends to zero over zero or infinity over infinity in the limit, the form is said to be indeterminate; these labels do not represent values, so an equation setting a limit equal to zero over zero is not a correct statement.
concepts.description_plain: Zero over zero and infinity over infinity are labels for a limit that is not yet settled, not values.
concepts.name: Indeterminate form
concepts.notation: the forms zero over zero and infinity over infinity

concepts.description_formal: Before L'Hospital's rule is applied the response must establish that the limits of the numerator and of the denominator are both zero, or that both are infinite; the CED unit overview states that students must verify this as a necessary first step.
concepts.description_plain: The rule may be used only after the form has been shown to be indeterminate.
concepts.name: The hypothesis of L'Hospital's rule
concepts.notation: separate limits of numerator and denominator

concepts.description_formal: Under the hypotheses, the limit of the quotient equals the limit of the quotient of the derivative of the numerator and the derivative of the denominator, which is not the derivative of the quotient.
concepts.description_plain: The rule replaces the limit of a ratio by the limit of the ratio of the two derivatives.
concepts.name: The conclusion of L'Hospital's rule
concepts.notation: limit of f prime over g prime

prerequisites.description_plain: Producing the volume of a cone, a sphere, and a cylinder, and the area of a circle, a triangle, and a rectangle, from the named dimensions.
prerequisites.failure_signature: No relating equation can be written, so the related rates setup never starts.
prerequisites.name: Volume and area formulas for standard solids
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements for this unit.

prerequisites.description_plain: Relating the two legs and the hypotenuse of a right triangle, and reading a word description into a right triangle.
prerequisites.failure_signature: A distance relation in a ladder, shadow, or approach problem cannot be written down.
prerequisites.name: The Pythagorean theorem and right triangle relations
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements for this unit.

prerequisites.description_plain: Setting up a proportion between corresponding sides of similar triangles and using it to eliminate one variable.
prerequisites.failure_signature: A cone or shadow problem keeps two varying dimensions and the differentiation cannot be completed.
prerequisites.name: Similar triangles and proportional reasoning
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements for this unit.

prerequisites.description_plain: Building and simplifying units such as degrees Celsius per minute or words per minute per minute, and attaching them to a reported value.
prerequisites.failure_signature: The numerical answer is correct and the unit is absent or is assembled the wrong way round.
prerequisites.name: Unit analysis with compound units
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements for this unit.

prerequisites.description_plain: Reading the absolute value of a signed quantity as its magnitude and knowing when the sign matters.
prerequisites.failure_signature: Speed is reported as a negative number, or a direction question is answered with a magnitude.
prerequisites.name: Absolute value as size without sign
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements for this unit.

prerequisites.description_plain: Writing the equation of a line through a point with a given slope and evaluating it at another input.
prerequisites.failure_signature: The tangent line approximation cannot be written, or is written with the point and the slope exchanged.
prerequisites.name: Point-slope form of a line
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements for this unit.

prerequisites.description_plain: Isolating one unknown in an equation whose other quantities are known numbers.
prerequisites.failure_signature: The differentiated relation is correct and the requested rate is never extracted from it.
prerequisites.name: Solving a linear equation for one unknown quantity
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements for this unit.

prerequisites.description_plain: Reading a description of a changing situation and naming each quantity, its unit, and whether it varies or is fixed.
prerequisites.failure_signature: The response cannot begin because the quantities in the scenario were never named; the CED unit overview records this translation as a recurring difficulty (ced:84).
prerequisites.name: Translating a verbal scenario into named variables
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements for this unit.

prerequisites.description_plain: Solving an equation for its zeros, splitting the interval at them, and determining the sign of the expression on each piece.
prerequisites.failure_signature: Intervals of motion or of increase are reported from sampled integer inputs rather than from the zeros of the expression.
prerequisites.name: Sign analysis of an expression over an interval
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements for this unit.
